title: Busy in ministry. Empty in spirit.
paragraphs:
Busy in ministry. Empty in spirit.
That is one of the most dangerous places a believer can stand—holding the microphone while quietly losing the oil.

You can preach and still be prayerless.
Serve and still be starving.
Lead worship and still feel no wonder.
Open your Bible for sermons… but not for your own soul.

That is not just exhaustion.
That is a warning.
Martha was busy with much serving, but Mary sat at the feet of Jesus. And Jesus did not shame service—He exposed distraction. “One thing is necessary” (Luke 10:38–42).

Some ministers are drowning in church work while neglecting Christ Himself.
Public fire.
Private ashes.

Jesus does not call the weary servant away to condemn him.
He calls him back to Himself.
“Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest” (Matthew 11:28).

You do not need a better schedule before you need a Savior.
You need repentance.
You need presence.
You need to stop confusing activity with intimacy.

Ministry without communion becomes performance.
Service without devotion becomes noise.
But when you return to Jesus, the burden lifts, the soul breathes, and the secret place becomes sweet again.

Brother, sister—God never asked you to carry His work without His presence.
Sit again at His feet.
Weep if you must.
Be still long enough for your heart to remember who you were serving in the first place.

You are not saved by ministry.
You are saved by Christ.
And the same Jesus who called you to serve is still calling you to abide.
Don’t just work for Him. Walk with Him.
